key_results: MT stabilization suppresses GEF-H1-dependent contractility, reduces cell stiffness, and increases transcellular pore formation in both normal and glaucomatous cells; pharmacological MT stabilization enhances outflow facility in ex vivo mouse eyes by ~30–50%
comments: Identifies MT-dependent signaling as a mechanotransduction bottleneck in glaucoma, with clear therapeutic implications, though in vivo efficacy and long-term effects remain to be demonstrated.

Mouse whole-eye perfusion

hypotheses.result: MT stability is reduced in glaucomatous cells and modulated by mechanical microenvironment

hypotheses.result: MT stabilization reduces cellular stiffness and promotes transcellular pore formation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Enhanced pore formation increases aqueous humor outflow
hypotheses.result: MT stabilization enhances conventional outflow facility in ex vivo eyes

task: Standardized residue numbering system for functionally diverse microbial rhodopsins
key_results: MO numbering system enables consistent residue mapping across 129 structures and ~40,000 sequences despite low sequence identity; successfully predicts sequence–structure–function relationships for previously uncharacterized rhodopsins
comments: This is primarily a bioinformatics resource rather than new experimental findings; its impact depends on community adoption for optogenetic engineering.

title: Pericyte-derived exosomal hexokinase 2 promotes retinal neovascularization via non-metabolic ELK3 upregulation
task: Characterize pericyte-derived exosomal HK2-mediated promotion of retinal neovascularization via non-metabolic ELK3 signaling
key_results: Hypoxic pericytes upregulate HK2 and release HK2-enriched exosomes; exosomal HK2 promotes endothelial growth in vitro; pericyte Hk2 deletion or exosome inhibition reduced neovascular tuft formation; exosomal HK2 increases mTOR activity and ELK3 levels; ELK3 is elevated in oxygen-induced retinopathy vascular tufts
comments: Reveals a non-canonical, non-metabolic function for HK2 in exosomal signaling that drives pathological angiogenesis, offering a new therapeutic angle distinct from glycolytic inhibition.

model_io.model: Pericytes, endothelial cells, and oxygen-induced retinopathy mouse model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Pericyte-derived HK2 promotes angiogenesis through metabolic reprogramming
hypotheses.result: Exosomal HK2 functions non-metabolically via mTOR-dependent ELK3 upregulation in endothelial cells

title: Targeting hepatocyte-derived LRG1 with dothiortone alleviates hepatic ischemia–reperfusion injury and remote renal damage via suppressing NETosis
task: Identify hepatocyte-derived LRG1 as a mediator of hepatic ischemia–reperfusion injury and remote renal damage via neutrophil NETosis
key_results: Proteomic profiling identified LRG1 as upregulated in mouse HIRI; hepatocyte-specific Lrg1 knockout reduced liver injury, inflammation, NET formation, and apoptosis; LRG1 binds TGFβR1 on neutrophils, activating SMAD3-driven Pad4 transcription and NETosis; NETs trigger AIM2-dependent hepatocyte apoptosis and renal tubular damage; dothiortone (mangrove-derived polyketide) inhibits LRG1 and mitigates HIRI and renal injury
comments: Establishes hepatocyte–neutrophil crosstalk via LRG1–TGFβR1 signaling as a driver of multiorgan injury, identifies dothiortone as a lead therapeutic candidate, and suggests NETosis inhibition as a strategy for ischemia–reperfusion syndromes.

model_io.model: Mouse HIRI model, hepatocytes, and neutrophils

hypotheses.hypothesis: HIRI-induced injury occurs through hepatocyte-intrinsic mechanisms
hypotheses.result: Hepatocyte-derived LRG1 drives NETosis via TGFβR1–SMAD3–PAD4 axis, and NETs propagate injury to both hepatocytes and kidneys through AIM2-dependent mechanisms

title: JNK signalling balances apoptosis and cell survival during tissue stress
task: Elucidate how JNK signaling orchestrates apoptosis and proliferation during epithelial tissue stress and recovery
key_results: Optogenetic JNK activation arrests proliferation and triggers apoptosis in wing primordia; JNK level does not correlate cell-by-cell with apoptosis; G1 cells undergo apoptosis with mild JNK, while G2-arrested cells are protected; JNK upregulates Dally/Dlp glypicans, enhancing Wnt/BMP ligand retention; Dlp reduction impairs recovery from ribosomal protein deficiency or irradiation
comments: Reveals that cell cycle phase gates JNK-dependent apoptosis and that JNK-induced protective morphogen signaling enables selective survival and tissue regeneration, providing a systems-level model of stress-response coordination.

model_io.model: Optogenetic Drosophila wing primordia

hypotheses.hypothesis: JNK directly triggers apoptosis proportionally to signaling intensity
hypotheses.result: JNK level does not predict apoptosis on a cell-by-cell basis; cell cycle phase and JNK-induced morphogen signaling gate apoptotic sensitivity and enable recovery

title: Bindarit ameliorates doxorubicin-induced ovarian damage by suppressing CCL8-dependent macrophage infiltration and NF-κB-mediated inflammation
task: Investigate CCL8-mediated inflammatory remodeling in doxorubicin-induced ovarian damage and therapeutic potential of Bindarit
key_results: DOX upregulates Ccl8, promoting M1-macrophage infiltration and NF-κB activation; Bindarit (localized ovarian delivery) reduced collagen, restored ovarian index by ~32%, decreased apoptosis, partially restored fertility; CCL8 knockdown suppressed inflammatory gene expression
comments: Localizes chemokine-mediated inflammation as a key driver of DOX toxicity and demonstrates that targeted inhibition prior to chemotherapy can preserve reproductive function, a clinically important finding for young cancer patients.

model_io.model: Mouse DOX-induced ovarian injury model and KGN granulosa cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: DOX-induced ovarian injury occurs through a single inflammatory pathway
hypotheses.result: CCL8-driven macrophage infiltration and NF-κB activation are central mechanisms; Bindarit intervention prior to DOX exposure mitigates damage

title: MBD3 D246-dependent Runx2–NuRD association promotes Runx2 deacetylation, osteoblast dysfunction, and glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis
task: Identify MBD3-dependent mechanisms regulating Runx2 deacetylation and osteoblast dysfunction in glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis
key_results: MBD3 upregulated in GIOP bone tissue; MBD3 associates with Runx2 and increases HDAC1–Runx2 interaction, reducing Runx2 acetylation; D246 is critical for MBD3–Runx2 binding; MBD3 knockdown restored acetyl lysine levels and trabecular bone in vivo; HDAC inhibitor SAHA partially reversed GIOP defects
comments: Identifies a chromatin remodeling-mediated mechanism of glucocorticoid toxicity and reveals D246 as a potentially druggable target for restoring osteoblast function through enhanced Runx2 acetylation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: MBD3 regulates osteoblast function independently of its chromatin remodeling complex role
hypotheses.result: MBD3 specifically enhances HDAC1–Runx2 association and deacetylation, impairing Runx2-driven osteogenic activity through NuRD-dependent mechanisms

title: Chemokine and opioid peptide scavenging through constitutive and ligand-induced release of ACKR3-bearing extracellular vesicles
task: Characterize ACKR3 release on extracellular vesicles and its role in ligand scavenging
key_results: ACKR3 is released on EVs both basally and upon ligand stimulation; EV-associated ACKR3 retains high-affinity binding and sequesters CXCL12 and opioid peptides, attenuating downstream signaling through CXCR4 and MOR
comments: Establishes EVs as a previously underappreciated dimension of GPCR-mediated ligand regulation with potential therapeutic implications for chemokine and opioid systems.

model_io.model: Multiple cellular systems (endogenous and transfected)

hypotheses.hypothesis: ACKR3 release on EVs is mechanistically distinct from canonical internalization
hypotheses.result: Basal and ligand-induced EV release are independent of GRKs and β-arrestin but rely on different trafficking routes and C-terminal determinants

title: Two distinct α2β1 integrin glycan interactions mediate cell entry of a picornavirus
task: Identify integrin α2β1 glycan interactions mediating picornavirus entry via ERAV
key_results: ERAV binds integrin α2β1 in its closed conformation via α2 β-propeller, α2 N112 high-mannose glycan, and β1 N269 sialylated glycan; all three interactions are required for efficient virus entry
comments: Reveals a previously unseen dual-glycan binding mechanism for viral entry, expanding understanding of virus–receptor glycan interactions and potentially informing therapeutics targeting these interactions.

model_io.model: HEK293T cells, equine fibroblasts, and cryo-EM

hypotheses.hypothesis: ERAV binds integrin α2β1 through protein contacts alone
hypotheses.result: ERAV requires both protein and glycan interactions with α2β1; α2 N112 high-mannose and β1 N269 sialylated glycans are independently necessary and collectively sufficient

title: Tau monomers and fibrils escape microglial clearance via distinct cellular mechanisms
task: Dissect microglial clearance mechanisms for extracellular tau monomers vs. fibrils
key_results: Tau monomers are internalized via LRP1 but recycled to extracellular space without degradation; tau fibrils adhere to cell surface via HSPG, triggering TLR4-mediated inflammation; APOE variants reduce tau uptake
comments: Explains why microglia fail to clear tau despite their scavenging capacity, highlighting mechanistically distinct escape routes that have implications for Alzheimer's disease pathology.

model_io.model: Human iPSC-derived microglia

hypotheses.hypothesis: Tau monomers and fibrils are cleared through the same microglial pathway
hypotheses.result: Monomers and fibrils use mechanistically distinct clearance pathways; monomers recycle while fibrils trigger surface-dependent inflammation

title: Positional replication fork instability drives PARP inhibitor cytotoxicity
task: Identify replication-fork lesions at specific genomic loci as key drivers of PARP inhibitor cytotoxicity in ESCO2-deficient cells
key_results: CRISPR screen identified ESCO2 loss as conferring PARPi hypersensitivity independent of HR deficiency; ESCO2 loss accumulates G-quadruplex (G4) structures at replication sites; PARP inhibition prevents PARP1-dependent TIMELESS and DDX11 engagement, causing G4 accumulation, DNA damage, and chromosomal instability; G4 lesions localize to pericentromeric fragile regions
comments: Reveals G4-mediated replication stress as a potent driver of PARPi hypersensitivity, implicating hard-to-replicate loci as previously unrecognized sensitivity determinants and suggesting ESCO2 as a synthetic lethality partner.

model_io.model: CRISPR screens, single-molecule imaging, and cancer cell lines

hypotheses.hypothesis: ESCO2 loss promotes PARPi sensitivity through defective homologous recombination
hypotheses.result: ESCO2 loss confers PARPi hypersensitivity independent of HR deficiency by promoting G4 accumulation at pericentromeric loci; PARP1–TIMELESS–DDX11 axis safeguards fork stability at these sites

title: Dingxiang Guanshitong suppresses ESCC progression by modulating TAK1/NF-κB/GLUT1-associated glycolytic reprogramming
task: Determine mechanism by which Dingxiang Guanshitong suppresses ESCC progression via TAK1/NF-κB signaling
key_results: DGST dose-dependently suppressed tumor growth, proliferation, migration, and invasion while promoting apoptosis; DGST reduced TAK1/IκBα/p65 phosphorylation, GLUT1/HK2/PFKP/LDHA expression, and ATP levels; TAK1 knockdown enhanced DGST effects, overexpression reversed them
comments: Links traditional herbal medicine to modern signaling pathways, demonstrating glycolytic reprogramming as a therapeutic target in ESCC and suggesting TAK1 as a key therapeutic nodal point.

hypotheses.hypothesis: DGST targets glycolysis through multiple independent mechanisms

title: Adipose derived small extracellular vesicles improve spermatogenesis and fertility in a mouse model of azoospermia compared with stem cell and combination therapies
task: Compare therapeutic efficacy of AD-MSCs, AD-MSC-derived sEVs, and their combination in a mouse azoospermia model
key_results: AD-MSC-sEVs showed greatest improvements in spermatogenesis-related gene expression, hormonal profiles, sperm quality, and fertility compared to AD-MSCs or combination; no GFP-positive spermatozoa or F1 testicular GFP detected
comments: Demonstrates superior efficacy of cell-free sEV therapy over cellular therapy, supporting sEVs as a viable clinical approach for NOA; absence of GFP in spermatozoa suggests paracrine rather than direct participation in germ-cell differentiation.

model_io.model: Busulfan-induced azoospermia mouse model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Combined AD-MSCs and sEVs provide superior benefit over single-component therapy
hypotheses.result: AD-MSC-sEVs alone showed greatest efficacy; combination therapy did not exceed sEV monotherapy under these experimental conditions

title: Weak electromagnetic field configuration differentially shapes cellular redox and metabolic responses
task: Determine whether weak electromagnetic field configuration determines cellular redox and metabolic responses independently of intensity
key_results: SF, RF, and full tNMR produced distinct redox-metabolic profiles: SF increased extracellular H₂O₂; RF increased NAD⁺/NADH ratio and reduced lactate; tNMR increased mitochondrial MitoSOX and total NADP(H); respiratory/glycolytic parameters remained comparable
comments: Field configuration, not intensity alone, governs cellular redox-metabolic responses, suggesting therapeutic tNMR efficacy may depend on precise component ratios rather than field strength alone.

model_io.model: NIH3T3 cells during hypoxia–reoxygenation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Weak electromagnetic field effects depend on field intensity
hypotheses.result: Field configuration, not intensity alone, is the key determinant; SF, RF, and tNMR produce distinct redox-metabolic profiles

title: A tumor-associated K318N variant abolishes AGGF1 nuclear import by disrupting key nucleocytoplasmic transport motifs
task: Identify nucleocytoplasmic transport motifs in AGGF1 and characterize a tumor-associated import-defective variant
key_results: Three motifs (272–279, 317–328, 509–519 aa) govern AGGF1 localization; K318N variant causes profound cytoplasmic mislocalization independent of CRM1 or 14-3-3; K318N impairs p53 binding, stabilization, and transactivation
comments: Single-residue variant disrupts nuclear import and p53-dependent tumor suppression, revealing how missense mutations can abolish nuclear localization signaling without affecting export or cytoplasmic retention machinery.

task: Assess metabolic changes in glioblastoma following combined temozolomide and lonidamine treatment using MR imaging/spectroscopy
key_results: LND + TMZ significantly reduced lactate levels and MCT4 expression vs. control/TMZ-only; acute decrease in mitochondrial respiration observed in vitro with partial recovery; enhanced but not statistically significant survival benefit

task: Determine mechanism by which MSC-derived exosomes protect against cadmium-induced hepatotoxicity
key_results: MSCs-Exos suppress mitochondria-dependent ferroptosis by restoring mitochondrial integrity, reducing ROS/iron accumulation, and rebalancing ferroptosis regulators; in vivo, MSCs-Exos home to injured liver and reduce liver enzymes, inflammation, and ultrastructural damage

title: Lactylation couples glycolysis with cell cycle progression in cancer cells
task: Determine mechanism linking glycolytic lactate production to Aurora B activation and mitotic progression in cancer
key_results: Lactate promotes KAT2A-mediated lactylation of PGK1 at K131; lactylated PGK1 phosphorylates Aurora B at T232, promoting cell cycle progression; PGK1 K131R mutation causes mitotic defects and cGAS–STING activation; PGK1–Aurora B disruption peptide combined with anti-PD-1 enhances CD8+ T-cell infiltration
comments: Establishes lactate as a metabolic–epigenetic hub coupling glycolysis to mitotic control, revealing a therapeutically targetable link between tumor metabolism and proliferation that also triggers immunogenic responses.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Aurora B activity is regulated independently of metabolic status
hypotheses.result: Lactate-dependent PGK1 lactylation couples glycolytic flux to Aurora B activation and mitotic progression

key_results: Weakly indirect band gap 5.029 eV; dielectric constant 3.636, refractive index 1.907; elastic anisotropy with directional Young's modulus along c-axis 539.19 GPa; elastic constants satisfy Born stability criteria
comments: Rigorous computational study with good structural validation; strong Si–N hybridization is well-characterized but high-pressure or temperature-dependent properties not explored.

model_io.model: DFT (CASTEP, rSCAN meta-GGA, DFT-D4) for β-Si₃N₄

hypotheses.hypothesis: β-Si₃N₄ wide-gap insulator with strong Si–N hybridization and mechanical anisotropy suitable for high-T and UV applications
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: band gap 5.03 eV, elastic anisotropy, and optical response all consistent with wide-gap ceramic behavior

title: Detector-optimized wavelength-hybrid entangled photon source for scalable fiber quantum key distribution
task: Optimize entangled photon source for fiber QKD via wavelength-hybrid design matching detector/transmission constraints
key_results: Type-0 ppKTP source at 680/1550 nm achieves spectral brightness (1.9×10³) s⁻¹ mW⁻¹ GHz⁻¹; polarization visibilities (97.3±1.0)% and (94.9±1.6)%; state fidelity ≥(96.1±1.3)%; 680 nm routed to Si-SPAD, 1550 nm through telecom fiber
comments: Well-engineered practical source balancing brightness, fidelity and infrastructure constraints; long-term stability and temperature sensitivity not reported.

model_io.model: Type-0 SPDC in ppKTP (crossed crystal, 473 nm pump)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Wavelength-hybrid architecture optimizes source for simultaneous low-loss transmission (1550 nm) and efficient detection (680 nm Si-SPAD)
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: high fidelity (96.1%) and brightness achieved; practical QKD node deployment feasibility demonstrated

title: Preliminary evaluation of inductive current transformers applicability for accurate transformation of distorted current
task: Assess inductive current transformer applicability for distorted current transformation
key_results: Excitation current RMS level correlates with harmonic self-generation; factor ranking matches 3rd/5th harmonic distortion when differences exceed 25%
comments: Method is indirect and only validated for 3rd/5th harmonics; broader harmonic coverage and real-world grid data would improve practical utility.

model_io.model: Inductive current transformer with nonlinear magnetic core

hypotheses.hypothesis: Core nonlinearity degree (via excitation current measurement) predicts secondary harmonic self-generation
hypotheses.result: Partially confirmed for 3rd/5th harmonics; ranking consistency achieved when distortion differences >25%

title: Assessment of round-trip and coulombic efficiency in lithium-ion batteries using a mathematical modeling approach under variable operating conditions
task: Model Coulombic efficiency and round-trip performance evolution in Li-ion batteries under aging and thermal stress
key_results: Capacity loss 34.1% (2.704→1.783 Ah) over 1500 cycles; Coulombic efficiency drops from 90.1% to 59.43%; model validated across 0–75 °C range
comments: Comprehensive experimental validation is valuable; mechanistic understanding of degradation pathways could be deepened with post-mortem characterization.

model_io.model: Li-ion battery analytical model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Coulombic efficiency, capacity retention and temperature follow coupled power-law or exponential degradation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: model shows good agreement with measured evolution across 1500 cycles and temperature range

title: A temporal graph transformer neural network for clustering influential control nodes in the controllability processes on of social internet of things networks
task: Identify influential control nodes in time-evolving multi-layer social IoT networks using temporal graph transformer
key_results: TGCIN achieves 91% average accuracy and 92% F1-score; partitions nodes into critical drivers, bridging relays, peripheral; faster convergence than competing methods; interpretable cluster distributions maintained on large-scale graphs
comments: Strong performance metrics and interpretability are valuable; comparison with recent graph neural network baselines (e.g., temporal point processes) would contextualize novelty.

model_io.model: TGCIN (Temporal Graph Transformer for Clustering Influential Nodes)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Relation-aware spatial attention + GRU temporal encoder + controllability-informed scoring identifies control roles accurately
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 91% accuracy and F1-score across tested scenarios; faster convergence than alternatives

title: Tailoring the nanoscale physicochemical properties of V2O5 thin films through Mn doping for enhanced electrochemical performance
task: Enhance electrochemical performance of V₂O₅ thin films via Mn doping
key_results: 4% Mn-doped V₂O₅ showed superior specific capacitance and charge-transfer kinetics in 5 M KOH; enhanced absorbance and reduced transmittance confirm defect-state formation; improved ohmic conductivity
comments: Sol-gel synthesis is cost-effective and results are electrochemically promising, but cycling stability and long-term durability data are absent.

model_io.model: Sol-gel synthesized Mn-doped V₂O₅ thin film on ITO

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mn doping creates oxygen vacancies and defect states, enhancing charge-storage capacity and conductivity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 4% doping optimizes lattice distortion and defect density for improved electrochemical performance

title: Fractal basin geometry and the limits to predictability and reproducibility in deep learning
task: Explain irreproducibility in deep learning via riddled basin geometry in parameter space
key_results: Minimal neural network model analytically derives classical riddling route with near-zero uncertainty exponent; intertwined training destinations and scale-insensitive irreproducibility observed across architectures and optimizers; functional uncertainty exponents extend diagnostics to learned functions
comments: Novel dynamical systems perspective on deep learning reproducibility is insightful; experimental validation on large-scale models and practical implications for hyperparameter tuning merit further exploration.

model_io.model: Deep neural network training dynamics

hypotheses.hypothesis: Riddled basin geometry with fat-fractal structure explains why initialization precision yields marginal gains in outcome predictability
hypotheses.result: Confirmed analytically and numerically: near-zero parameter-space exponent observed across tested architectures and protocols

title: Interplay of superconductivity and ferromagnetism in ferromagnetic-semiconductor-based Josephson junctions
task: Explore superconductivity–ferromagnetism interplay in Al/InAs/(Ga,Fe)Sb Josephson junctions
key_results: Gate-tunable supercurrents with multiple Andreev reflections observed; unconventional Fraunhofer patterns showing hysteresis, flux jumps, asymmetry, and nonreciprocity consistent with time-reversal symmetry breaking and induced ferromagnetism
comments: Clear signatures of unusual proximity effects, though direct microscopic confirmation of edge-channel transport or ferromagnetic induction mechanisms would strengthen interpretation.

model_io.model: Al/InAs/(Ga,Fe)Sb heterostructure Josephson junction

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ferromagnetic semiconductor induces time-reversal symmetry breaking and nonreciprocal Josephson effects
hypotheses.result: Confirmed qualitatively: unconventional interference patterns and asymmetry observed under magnetic field

title: Insect-inspired hexapod robot with magnetically coupled compliant and modular drive system
task: Design magnetically coupled modular hexapod robot with intrinsic mechanical compliance and fault tolerance
key_results: INSECTRON achieves minimum Cost of Transport 30; >90% autonomous recovery from vertical perturbations; tool-free leg replacement and rapid reconfiguration enabled; stable locomotion across multiple slopes/substrates with differential turning
comments: Elegant bio-inspired magnetic design reduces complexity; terrain and payload diversification would strengthen evidence for scalability.

model_io.model: INSECTRON hexapod with magnetic couplings and phase-domain controller

hypotheses.hypothesis: Magnetic transmission acts as intrinsic mechanical preflex, enabling rapid perturbation responses without active control
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: >90% recovery rate demonstrates passive impact tolerance; autonomous coordination via Hall-effect sensing sufficient

title: Single-particle limit of a topological edge state in a locally resonant band gap
task: Collapse topological edge state to single-particle mode via local resonance singularity in SSH-inspired system
key_results: Local resonator creates attenuation singularity; tuning dimerization parameter migrates singularity between gaps via flat-band intermediate state while preserving band topology; edge state collapsing to singularity yields inverse participation ratio unity (theoretical localization limit); single-particle mode stable over broad parameter range under boundary tuning despite disorder
comments: Elegant topological–resonance interplay achieving extreme localization at low frequencies is conceptually novel; experimental demonstration in acoustic or mechanical metamaterials would validate predictions.

model_io.model: 1D SSH-inspired stiffness dimer with local resonator

hypotheses.hypothesis: Attenuation singularity in local-resonance band gap can transfer topological edge state character to single-particle confinement
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: edge mode collapses to IPR=1 (single-particle limit) when intersecting singularity; stability preserved via boundary tuning

title: Chimney-board metastructures for birefraction and asymmetric transmission of water waves
task: Achieve broadband birefraction and asymmetric transmission of water waves using chimney-board metastructure
key_results: Chimney-board metastructure creates double modes for low-frequency water waves; effective refractive index difference 1.55; refracted beam separation >40°; broadband asymmetric transmission blocks destructive incoming waves while allowing harbor-generated waves to escape; demonstrates proof-of-concept for harbor protection
comments: First experimental realization of water-wave birefraction is notable; frequency-dependent performance and scaling to ocean-scale applications need exploration.

model_io.model: Chimney-board metastructure for water waves

hypotheses.hypothesis: Stratified metastructure supporting two-mode propagation enables high-order lattice birefraction and tunable asymmetric transmission
hypotheses.result: Confirmed experimentally: refraction angle >40°, effective index difference 1.55; asymmetric transmission demonstrated for harbor protection scenario

title: Personalization and evaluation of human whole-body metabolic models and community microbiome models using Persephone
task: Personalize and integrate human whole-body metabolic models with microbiome community models
key_results: Persephone pipeline enables non-expert personalization of WBMs using physiological and metabolomic data; processing 100 metagenomic samples takes several days to weeks on single computer
comments: The standardized pipeline significantly lowers barriers to entry, though computational scalability remains challenging for large cohorts.

model_io.model: Persephone personalization pipeline

hypotheses.hypothesis: Physiological parameters like body weight significantly affect predicted human metabolism
hypotheses.result: Evaluable through Persephone statistical analyses; results visualized but not quantified in abstract

title: A microfluidic mother machine for high-throughput single-cell analysis of human leukemia T cells
task: Characterize single-cell T-cell proliferation dynamics via microfluidic tracking
key_results: Successfully tracked human leukemia T-cells over multiple generations; revealed slightly asymmetric volume division using sizer-like compensation strategy
comments: Computational fluid dynamics optimization for device geometry is sound, though the biological insight is descriptive rather than mechanistic.

model_io.model: Mother machine microfluidic device

hypotheses.hypothesis: T-cells employ a sizer-like strategy to regulate cell division
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; cells show asymmetric division compensating for size stochasticity
